doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Getting the Ellington job in 1926; hearing Bechet at the Kentucky Club
summary: Duke asked Carter to fill in on saxophone; Carter recalls having heard the band with Bubber Miley and Sidney Bechet at the Kentucky Club.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Okay. Yeah, I think before we move on to Fletcher Henderson and your longer stint with him, which came later, just touch on that . . . you brought up a short stay with Duke Ellington, which was also in 1926. I think it was a little earlier than your subbing for Don Redmond with Fletcher Henderson.
How did you get the gig, so to speak?
I don’t know. They needed a saxophone player, and Duke contacted me.
You obviously must have known each other by then, to some extent.

Yes, in . . . you know, I don’t know. I don’t know when he’d heard me, because I had heard his group, oh, gee, they played at a place called the Kentucky Club, and I think they had Sidney Bachet on soprano. Now, how I got in there, one of the musicians must have taken me or something, but I remember going there, you know. I was probably backstage or something, or hidden behind a curtain or something, or maybe waiting, wearing a waiter’s uniform and carrying a tray or something. [laughter] Not really, but, you know, I wasn’t there as a paying guest at a table. But I remember being there. I wonder who could have taken me? Oh, was Bubber Miley playing with them there? That would have been it. That would have been it, of course. Yes, yes, at the Kentucky Club.
Yes, Bubber Miley, Bachet, Charlie Irvis on trombone. That was before Johnny Hodges.
Did Bachet and Johnny Hodges ever play together?
I don’t think they were in the same time.
What sort of impression did you have of Bachet? This was a very kind of different . . .

Oh, it was different. Well, it was exciting, you know. I probably didn’t know enough about music to analyze what he was doing, you know, in a broad sense, but I liked it, you know. He was saying something.
